subject.title: Newark — Measure DD (Newark Essential Services Protection Measure)

text: “Newark Essential Services Protection Measure. To protect city services such as repairing potholes/streets; keeping neighborhoods safe/clean, and maintaining 9-1-1 emergency response/fire protection/ neighborhood police patrols/parks/recreation programs, shall the measure be adopted updating Newark’s 56-year- old business license ordinance, lowering many small businesses' taxes, with rates up to 0.3% of gross receipts (as described in the ordinance), raising $6,600,000 annually until ended by voters, with spending disclosure/ independent audits?”

The City Council of the City of Newark is submitting to the voters the question of whether to approve an ordinance that would repeal and replace the existing business license tax codified in Newark Municipal Code Chapter 5.04. The City imposes a business license tax on businesses conducting business within the City. The current business license tax sorts businesses into multiple categories based on business type. Currently, the tax is a flat tax, a tax based on number of employees, a tax based on number of vehicles, a tax based on a percentage of payroll or a tax based on a percentage of gross receipts, depending on the category. If approved, Measure DD would amend the business license tax to consolidate the existing categories into seven categories, with all business types paying a tax based on a percentage of gross receipts, with the rate depending on the category. Measure DD includes a business license tax exemption category for various activities, including activities by not-for-profit entities.
If approved, Measure DD would establish the following business categories and tax rates, which are percentages of a business’s annual gross receipts: General Retail and Restaurants – 0.0003; Professional Services – 0.0025; Contractors and Services – 0.002; Rental (Commercial and Residential), Self-Storage, Hotels, Motels and Short-Term Rentals – 0.00075; Manufacturing, Wholesaling and Importing/Exporting of Goods – 0.00075; and Distribution and Logistics – 0.003. Businesses are required to pay a minimum tax amount irrespective of gross receipts. Measure DD would change the minimum tax paid by all categories from a flat amount of $39 to a flat amount of $25 on the first $100,000 of gross receipts, which would result in a tax reduction for some businesses.
Measure DD would provide that the repeal and replacement of the business license tax would be implemented on January 1, 2027. The business license tax would continue to be ongoing if Measure DD is approved.
Because Measure DD does not limit the use of business license tax revenue, it is a “general tax,” and the funds provided are available for any legitimate governmental purpose. As noted in the ballot question, examples of uses of revenue from the business license tax include street and pothole repairs, keeping neighborhoods safe and clean, and maintaining 9-1-1 emergency response, fire protection, neighborhood police patrols, parks and recreation programs. Measure DD would generate approximately $6.6 million in funds annually that are legally required to be used in Newark to support city services.
A “Yes” vote is a vote to approve adopting an ordinance that would repeal and replace the existing business license tax. A “No” vote is a vote against adopting the ordinance. Measure DD will be approved if it receives a simple majority of “Yes” votes from those voting on the Measure.
DATED: August 5, 2026

text:
The argument for this tax increase is deceptive and inaccurate.
This $5.5 million (465%) tax increase would harm Newark. It is counterproductive and unfair, and the money could be used without restrictions. Please vote NO on Measure DD. Resources for roads, public safety and emergency response can be best assured by supporting small businesses and attracting new businesses—not by squeezing Newark businesses. The best way to increase revenue is to grow our economy, not raise taxes.
The argument in favor, and the measure title of this tax increase implies that the funds would be used for specific purposes. This is untrue. This would be a general tax, meaning the funds can be used for any legal purpose the City Council chooses-including City Council compensation and / or executive salaries.
The argument also states that the money must be spent locally. This statement is inaccurate. This tax revenue can be spent for any legal purpose the City Council authorizes, including purposes outside Newark.
This tax increase would hurt Newark businesses and ultimately be passed on to residents through higher prices. Such a large tax increase would harm Newark’s economy and residents. It is counterproductive and unfair, and it would give the City Council greater control over funds that could be spent for virtually any legal purpose rather than defined priorities.
Please vote NO on Measure DD.

text:
The City Council voted to place a 465% increase in the Business License Tax on the ballot. This represents a $5 million increase in taxation. I am a member of the Newark City Council, and I was the only councilmember to vote against it because I believe it would undermine the economic health of our community.
While it is true that our city needs revenue to provide quality services, safe neighborhoods, and well-maintained streets and parks, this tax increase would hinder economic growth and ultimately constrain future revenue. It would place an additional financial burden on local businesses at a time when many are already struggling with rising costs for supplies, rent, utilities, wages, insurance, and federal tariffs. As a result, businesses may be forced to raise prices to offset the increased tax burden.
This tax increase would harm our business community, slow job growth, raise prices, and make it more difficult to retain existing businesses and attract new ones to Newark. A healthy local economy benefits everyone. Policies that increase the cost of doing business risk slowing economic growth and making it harder for businesses to thrive. Supporters of this tax increase promise new revenue for important city priorities, but this measure is a general tax and does not guarantee that the funds will be spent on the purposes described in the ballot measure. Instead, the revenue could be used for any governmental purpose. There are better ways to strengthen the city’s finances without placing additional burdens on local employers and residents. For example, encouraging business growth and resolving the challenges at NewPark Mall could help generate additional revenue without raising tax rates. For these reasons, I urge you to vote
on this Business License Tax increase.
